key_insight: In TiO2-terminated SrTiO3(001), the OER activity is strongly controlled by the Fermi-level-dependent charge state of Fe dopants and oxygen vacancies, making defect chemistry a direct knob for overpotential.
engineering_relevance: This suggests defect and Fermi-level engineering can be used to tune perovskite oxide electrocatalysts, but the same defect can help or hurt OER depending on its charge state and segregation behavior.
method: First-principles DFT for Fe dopants and oxygen vacancies on SrTiO3(001).
Charge-dependent defect formation energies, segregation energies, and charge transition levels.
Computational hydrogen electrode free-energy profiles for OER intermediates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports quantified overpotentials across defect states: near-pristine behavior for neutral FeTi and pristine surfaces (~0.43–0.48 V vs 0.45 V), but much worse activity for reduced Fe states and some vacancy states (up to 2.13 V).
watch_item: Activity depends on whether defects are surface-segregated and on the assumed charge state, so real-device performance will be sensitive to operating Fermi level, termination, and defect distributions.
paper_title: Fermi-Level-Dependent Defect Chemistry and Oxygen Evolution Reaction Activity of Fe-Doped and Oxygen-Deficient \ce{SrTiO3}(001)
